candidate.title: iCLIP
candidate.scope: The single-route Illumina iCLIP schematic, from the RNA–protein complex to PCR-amplified cDNA. The leftmost iCLIP icon is a descriptive title, not a separate sample branch. UV crosslinking and the separate RNA 3′-adapter interface are resolved from the cited iCLIP primary paper; no alternative workflow is drawn. The collection page heading and caption also identify iCLIP. Its extra labels and the card’s discussion of HITS-CLIP, PAR-CLIP, eCLIP and irCLIP do not expand the assigned PNG’s target scope.

operations.label: Crosslink (primary-resolved part of the first transition)
operations.description: UV irradiation converts an associated RNA–protein complex into a covalently attached complex before immunoprecipitation. The assigned PNG omits a separate crosslink caption but shows crosslink marks in the captured product.
operations.mechanism: UV-induced covalent protein–RNA crosslinking, as reported for iCLIP.
operations.information_effect: Fixes the RNA–protein contact as the covalent association that later survives as an RNA-bound peptide.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate cross-linked RNA-protein complex
operations.description: Antibody capture enriches crosslinked complexes containing the chosen protein; the output is an immunoprecipitated RNA–protein complex.

operations.information_effect: Associates recovered RNA with the immunoprecipitated protein; nonspecific antibody capture remains possible.

operations.label: RNA 3′-adapter ligation (primary-resolved interface)
operations.description: A separate RNA adapter is ligated to the captured RNA’s 3′ end to provide the RNA-side interface for reverse transcription. This addition has no distinct caption or arrow in the assigned PNG; the primary paper places it after capture and before proteolysis.
operations.mechanism: Ligation of an RNA adapter to the RNA 3′ end; no unshown end-treatment sequence is asserted.
operations.information_effect: Provides a common priming interface without replacing the biological RNA sequence.

operations.label: Proteinase K
operations.description: The captured protein is digested, yielding recoverable RNA carrying a covalently attached peptide at the crosslink. The output is not naked RNA and does not retain an intact bulk protein.
operations.mechanism: Proteinase K digestion leaves a covalently bound polypeptide fragment.
operations.information_effect: Converts the captured protein contact into a local physical block on the RNA template.

operations.label: cDNA truncates at binding site
operations.description: Reverse transcription copies the RNA from the adapter interface and extends the cleavable, adapter-bearing RT oligonucleotide. The residual peptide causes premature termination; the output cDNA contains the copied RNA segment up to the stop, plus primer-derived regions.
operations.mechanism: Peptide-associated crosslinks impede RT; the retained cDNA truncation is exploited rather than requiring RT read-through.
operations.information_effect: Transfers RNA sequence and a positional boundary to DNA. The primer’s random barcode can distinguish original cDNA molecules from PCR duplicates in the primary implementation.

operations.label: Circularize

operations.label: Linearize and PCR
operations.description: The cDNA circle is opened within its primer-derived cleavable adapter segment, and the resulting linear cDNA is PCR-amplified to yield the final cDNA library. The drawing combines linearization and amplification in one block.
operations.mechanism: The primary implementation cuts at the BamHI site between the adapter regions, then amplifies with adapter-complementary primers.
operations.information_effect: Makes the barcode and RT-stop boundary readable in the final library. The primary paper defines the nucleotide immediately upstream of a mapped cDNA as the crosslink nucleotide; peptide steric effects can shift RT stops, so the red mark is not proof of a chemically exact contact in every molecule.

method_scopes.rationale: The PNG title, catalogue card and matching collection-page caption identify iCLIP as the only workflow target. The primary iCLIP full text supports its capture → residual peptide → truncated cDNA → circularization → linearization/PCR architecture. Crosslinking and RNA-adapter ligation are explicit paper-supported interfaces resolving the first transition and the RT substrate; they are not imported from the collection page’s expanded drawing. This extraction does not assign the route to HITS-CLIP, PAR-CLIP, eCLIP or irCLIP, and does not claim complete implementation identity with later protocols or applications. The collection-only footnotes to eCLIP and irCLIP are assessed as background references about unshown workflows; no publication-content sources for those footnotes were supplied.
